name: Queen of All Saints Basilica
history: A Catholic club pushed for a church in Chicago's Sauganash area in 1929, and Queen of All Saints parish was dedicated that June. The area filled with homes after World War II, largely Irish and German families. The present church was completed in 1960, and Pope John XXIII named it a basilica on 26 March 1962.
arch: A Neo-Gothic church by Meyer and Cook in Wisconsin Lannon stone and Indiana limestone with a Vermont slate roof, with a slender spire on its tower.
features: The great window over the choir loft shows eight Marian shrines, from Częstochowa and Knock to Guadalupe, Lourdes and Fatima.
A 60-rank Berghaus organ was installed in 2006.

look.d: The great window links the shrines of many peoples.
The slender spire rises over leafy Sauganash.

fun: One of only three basilicas in Chicago, and the youngest of them.
journal: Mid-century Gothic in Sauganash. One window, eight Marys from around the world.

quiz.q: How many Marian shrines appear in the great window?
